registers.name: FORMAT
registers.label: EEPROM format
registers.hint: The layout version of the radio's own settings store. Set by the firmware and not editable.

registers.name: SERIAL_SPEED
registers.label: Baud rate
registers.hint: The speed of the wire between this radio and whatever it is plugged into: the ground station here, the autopilot's telemetry port at the far end. It does not have to match the other radio, but it does have to match what is on the other end of its own cable.

registers.name: AIR_SPEED
registers.label: Air data rate
registers.hint: The speed the two radios talk to each other at. Lower reaches further and carries less: 64 kbps is the default and manages a kilometre or more on the small antennas the radios ship with.

registers.name: NETID
registers.label: Network ID
registers.hint: Which pair of radios this is. Two pairs on the same ID in the same field will interfere; give each aircraft its own number. It also seeds the frequency-hopping pattern, so different IDs hop differently.

registers.name: TXPOWER
registers.label: Transmit power
registers.hint: Check this against the limit where you are flying, and remember that the limit is on radiated power, and antenna gain counts towards it. The default of 20 dBm is inside the US and Australian 915 MHz allowance with an antenna below 10 dBi.

registers.name: ECC
registers.label: Error correction
registers.hint: Golay forward error correction: halves the usable bandwidth and recovers bit errors that would otherwise drop the packet. Newer radio chips cannot do it at all and will fail to run with it on, which is why current guidance is to leave it off.

registers.name: MAVLINK
registers.label: MAVLink framing
registers.hint: Aligns radio packets to MAVLink message boundaries so a lost packet does not deliver half a message. Leave this on MAVLink framing: RSSI and error reporting only arrive in that mode. Low latency additionally fast-tracks RC override, which is what a joystick flies on.

options.label: Low latency: prioritise RC override packets

registers.name: OPPRESEND
registers.label: Opportunistic resend
registers.hint: Resend a packet when the transmit window would otherwise go unused.

registers.name: MIN_FREQ
registers.label: Minimum frequency
registers.hint: The bottom of the band the radio hops within. A 433 MHz radio accepts 414000 to 454000 and a 900 MHz one 895000 to 935000; what you may actually use inside that is set by your national regulator.

registers.name: MAX_FREQ
registers.label: Maximum frequency
registers.hint: The top of the hopping band. Must be above the minimum, and the span between them is divided into the hopping channels.

registers.name: NUM_CHANNELS
registers.label: Hopping channels
registers.hint: How many frequencies the band is split into. More than one is what makes the radio frequency-agile, which several regulators require alongside listen-before-talk.

registers.name: DUTY_CYCLE
registers.label: Duty cycle
registers.hint: The share of the time this radio is allowed to transmit. 100 unless your regulator trades duty cycle for band or power. Europe's 433 MHz allowance below 10% is the usual reason. Zero makes the radio receive-only.

registers.name: LBT_RSSI
registers.label: Listen before talk
registers.hint: Wait for the channel to be quiet before transmitting. 0 disables it; the lowest working threshold is 25, and each step above that is about 0.5 dB over the receiver's noise floor.

registers.name: MANCHESTER
registers.label: Manchester encoding
registers.hint: Alternative line coding. Off unless something specific requires it.

registers.name: RTSCTS
registers.label: Hardware flow control
registers.hint: RTS/CTS on the serial wire. Worth enabling on a Pixhawk TELEM port, which carries the two extra pins; a radio on a USB cable does not.

registers.name: MAX_WINDOW
registers.label: Maximum transmit window
registers.hint: The longest a radio may hold the air before handing over. 131 is the default and gives the most bandwidth; 33 bounds how long a command from the ground can wait, which is what low-latency joystick control needs.

registers.name: ENCRYPTION_LEVEL
registers.label: Encryption
registers.hint: AES link encryption on the firmware builds that carry it. Both ends need the same level and the same key; the key is set with AT&E and is not readable back.

S6: MAVLINK=1

S15:MAX_WINDOW=131
S16: FOO = 7
S3=NETID=-4
